annotations.text:
Clickable prototype of the Sentinel console page (tech-specs/2026-09-sentinel).

Try it:
· Filter Open / Regressed / Ignored / Resolved, pick a worker, search.
· Click a row to open the group. Four tabs; the queue row is the log-source shape — a log record, no span tree.
· Investigate ▾ → Investigate opens the harness session in the second column and the first pass runs while you watch. Type in the composer to steer it, then Update diagnosis.
· Resolve ▾ and Ignore ▾ carry their scopes; the state changes and the list reorders.
· Close the session column, or go back to Groups, while the first pass runs — it keeps running; Open session brings the column back. Resolve while a diagnosis is pending — the record lands and the state stays.
· The gear opens the configuration form. The light/dark tweak sits above the frame.

What the prototype is arguing:

1. Nothing runs unsupervised. The click starts it, the session is visible beside the page, and Stop is one click away — which is why there are no turn, token or cost caps anywhere in the UI.

2. The record is structured even though the process is a conversation. The agent writes it by calling sentinel::diagnosis::record — no JSON turn, no output contract. v1 comes from the first pass at medium confidence with its gap named, v2 after you tell the agent what it could not see. A record never undoes a human decision: resolve or ignore while one is pending and the state stays.

3. Triage never pretends to be a diagnosis. It is one labelled hypothesis and where to look, with no code access.

Sample data throughout; the fingerprints, versions and traces are invented.
